text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Anglican Archbishop David Gitari will lead a nine-member religious committee to mediate in talks on constitutional reforms between the government, a civic lobby group and the opposition.
- The energy ministry says the World Bank has not cancelled any loan pledged to the energy sector.
- The government is given a 10-day ultimatum by opposition leaders to release 200 people arrested in violence following pro-reform rallies.
- Two armed robbers are shot dead by police in Nairobi after trying to free a prisoner from a hospital.
- President Daniel arap Moi urges western countries to be impartial in their assessment of Kenya's political development.
- The Food and Agriculture Organisation says tight food supply in Kenya is the main cause of a sharp increase in food prices.
- Nairobi mayor Dick Waweru is stripped off his executive powers by the council.
- A 45-year-old woman is jailed for 20 months for impersonating a voter registration office.

- Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi says he has forwarded to police for investigation 11 clearing and forwarding agents suspected of dumping sugar imports on the Kenyan market. ($1=70.17 Kenyan Shillings)
